lessonRef.subject: financial-literacy
lessonRef.title: Unit assessment: student aid grants scholarships and loans
lessonRef.focus: student aid grants scholarships and loans

objective: Learners complete an invented education-funding assessment, computing the borrowing gap, annual interest, and the long-run repayment total.
scenario: Orsolya is an invented eighth grader completing a pretend assessment: study costing $32,000.00, invented aid of $18,000.00, and the remainder borrowed at 5.5% simple interest, repaid over ten simulated years.
safetyNotes: Every amount, person, business, and account in this task is invented for practice. Nothing here refers to a real household.
Never write a real bank account, card, PIN, password, Social Security, or tax number on this sheet; the task never asks for one.
This is education, not individualized financial advice. Real money decisions belong to a trusted adult.

tasks.directions: Compute the borrowing gap in Orsolya's invented case after the aid is applied.
Compute one year of interest on that borrowing, then the total interest across ten simulated years.

prompts.text: What does one year of interest cost?
What does ten years of interest come to?

tasks.directions: Compute the total repaid over the ten years and what it would be if aid rose by $4,000.00.

prompts.text: What is repaid in total over ten years?
With $4,000.00 more aid, what would ten years of interest come to?

tasks.directions: Four thousand dollars of aid removed more than four thousand dollars of cost.

prompts.text: Quantify how much total cost the extra aid removes in Orsolya's case, and explain why aid is worth more than its face value.

remediation: If a learner applies the rate to the total cost, mark only Orsolya's borrowed gap as the base before any interest is computed.
extension: Ask the learner what aid level would keep Orsolya's total repayment under $15,000.00, and to show the method.
